d:
The Pulao vs Biryani debate has simmered in Indian kitchens for generations - some swear by the grandeur of Biryani, others stand firmly by the quiet confidence of Pulao.
This episode, we settle into Pulao’s camp.
Mutton Yakhni Pulao skips the layering and the dum. Instead, the meat is gently boiled into a fragrant Yakhni (stock), and the rice is cooked directly in it, letting every grain absorb the flavour from within.
Just a one-pot dish built on patience, served straight from the pot with a side of Burhani.
